title: Unbundling and Duplicate Billing

sections.learningObjectives:
- Define unbundling and duplicate billing and distinguish them from legitimate billing practices.
- Recognize improper billing practices, including unbundling and duplicate claims, in common office scenarios.
- Apply coding-edit and documentation principles to avoid billing errors.
- Identify the compliance, audit, and overpayment obligations tied to improper billing.
- Follow policy and escalate suspected billing errors to coding, billing, or compliance staff.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of a sandwich. Unbundling is like charging separately for the bread, the cheese, and the ham when the menu already lists one price for the whole sandwich.

### Question 2

Duplicate billing is like mailing the same birthday card to a friend twice by accident, so they think you sent two gifts. You should only send it once.

### Question 3

Unbundling is like a restaurant charging you for a burger and then charging you again for the bun and the patty that already come with it.

### Question 4

Sending the same letter both by email and by regular mail, so the person gets two copies of the same letter, is like duplicate billing.

### Question 5

A comprehensive code is like a combo meal at a restaurant, one price that already includes the sandwich, fries, and drink.

### Question 6

If a combo meal already includes fries, asking to also be charged for fries a second time is like unbundling.

### Question 7

Bundling is putting puzzle pieces together into one picture; unbundling is pulling the pieces back apart and charging for each one separately.

### Question 8

A duplicate is like the same movie ticket being scanned twice. If all the details match, it is probably the same ticket shown twice.

### Question 9

CMS is like the referee who makes the rulebook that tells offices which codes cannot be listed together on the same claim.

### Question 10

Coding edits are like a spell-checker for bills. They flag combinations that do not look right before the bill goes out.

### Question 11

A global surgical package is like buying a concert ticket that includes parking and the show all in one price.

### Question 12

If the concert ticket already includes the show, you do not pay again when you walk through the door for the encore.

### Question 13

A lab panel is like a value meal. You order the meal once, not each food item on its own.

### Question 14

Selling a cookie pack one cookie at a time instead of selling the whole pack at once is like unbundling a lab panel.

### Question 15

If a movie ticket already includes a drink, you do not buy a separate drink ticket, unless you are buying something extra that is truly different.

### Question 16

You cannot turn in homework you did not actually do. A code is like homework, and the chart note is the proof it was done.

### Question 17

Charge entry is like copying numbers from a recipe exactly. You do not add extra ingredients that were not in the recipe.

### Question 18

If a store accidentally gives you two toys when you paid for one, you have to give one back. The extra toy is not really yours.

### Question 19

If you mailed a letter and have not heard back, you check whether it arrived before mailing the same letter again.

### Question 20

Claim scrubbing is like a proofreader checking your essay for mistakes before you hand it in.

### Question 21

Unbundling is cutting one big cookie into crumbs and selling each crumb; upcoding is calling a small cookie a large one.

### Question 22

A corrected claim is like fixing a typo on a form and handing it in again; a duplicate is handing in the same form twice with no changes.

### Question 23

Splitting one big Lego castle into separate bricks and selling each brick on its own, when it should be sold as one castle, is like split-billing unbundling.

### Question 24

A modifier is like a sticky note added to a form that explains something extra, like writing 'this part was done separately' on the form.

### Question 25

You can only write 'done separately' on the form if the work really was done separately and you can show it was.

### Question 26

If the recipe says one cup of flour, you do not pour two cups and hope for the best. You measure exactly what the recipe says.

### Question 27

If a teammate asks you to cheat on a test, the right move is to say no and tell a trusted adult, not to help cheat.

### Question 28

If you buy a value meal, you pay for the value meal, not for each item separately plus the meal.

### Question 29

If a video game says you already used a code, you check your history first instead of typing the same code again with different numbers.

### Question 30

If a toy already comes with batteries included, you do not buy a second pack of batteries for it.

### Question 31

If you order a meal and also buy a completely different dessert that is not included, the dessert gets its own line on the receipt.

### Question 32

If two kids both turn in the exact same homework with the same name and date, the teacher knows one copy is extra.

### Question 33

Emailing a photo and also mailing a printed copy means the person receives the same photo twice.

### Question 34

If you made a mistake on a form, you erase and fix the same form instead of filling out a whole new one and handing in both.

### Question 35

If a spelling checker flags a word, you do not just click ignore on everything; you look at the word to decide.

### Question 36

A combo meal exists so you can order one thing instead of ten separate items for the same meal.

### Question 37

If the coach suggests cheating to win, the right move is to say no and tell a trusted adult, even if the coach is in charge.

### Question 38

If a cashier gives you too much change, the honest thing is to return the extra coins, not keep them.

### Question 39

An internal audit is like checking your homework answers afterward to catch mistakes before the teacher grades them.

### Question 40

You copy down only the items you actually put in the cart, not extra items you wish you had.

### Question 41

If you see a mistake that could get someone in trouble, you tell a teacher instead of covering it up.

### Question 42

Erasing the date on your homework and turning it in twice as if it were new is still turning in the same homework twice.

### Question 43

If you buy two apples, the receipt shows 'apples x2' on one line, not two separate receipts for one apple each.

### Question 44

If you see someone breaking the rules over and over, you tell a teacher quietly instead of ignoring it or joining in.

### Question 45

Knowing the rules of a game helps you play it correctly and notice when someone else is not.

### Question 46

A recipe book helps everyone bake the same cake correctly, instead of everyone guessing with different ingredients.

### Question 47

A suggestion box lets you share a problem without writing your name on it, so you feel safe telling the truth.

### Question 48

If you are not sure how to solve a math problem, you ask the teacher instead of guessing an answer.

### Question 49

If a teacher marks a wrong answer, you find the mistake and fix it, you do not keep turning in the same wrong answer.

### Question 50

If a friend says you charged them twice, you check the receipt together and fix it, you do not just insist they pay.

### Question 51

A homework check can happen both at your desk and at the teacher's desk, two chances to catch a mistake.

### Question 52

If you find a lost wallet, you return it right away; you do not wait for the owner to come looking.

### Question 53

You always proofread your essay before turning it in, so the teacher does not find silly mistakes.

### Question 54

If a phone comes with a case included, the case is covered, but a completely different accessory you buy separately is its own purchase.

### Question 55

If your phone is under a repair plan and you also get a totally different problem fixed, the second fix can be its own bill.

### Question 56

Charging extra for things that should be free is against the rules, like charging a fee for a door that comes with the house.

### Question 57

Turning off your smoke alarm so it stops beeping does not put out the fire; it just hides the warning.

### Question 58

If you resend a fixed version of a form, you write 'corrected' on it so no one thinks you sent the same form twice.

### Question 59

If two grown-ups share the cost of your lunch, the first one pays their part, then the second one pays the rest, not both paying the whole amount.

### Question 60

Sending the same letter twice does not make it arrive faster; it just gives the person two copies.

### Question 61

A checklist of which letters you already mailed stops you from mailing the same letter twice.

### Question 62

If the computer says you already turned in your homework, you stop and check instead of turning it in again.

### Question 63

Using a 'skip the rules' stamp when the work was not actually done separately is like faking a hall pass.

### Question 64

The assistant is like the person who helps set the table, while the chef decides what goes on each plate.

### Question 65

Charging two different people the full price for the same single lunch is like double-billing.

### Question 66

If the store says you already paid, you check your receipt before paying again.

### Question 67

Learning the updated rules of a game helps you play it fairly and notice when the rules change.

### Question 68

Accidentally mailing a card twice is a mistake, but mailing it twice on purpose to get two gifts is cheating.

### Question 69

If you cheat on an official test, you can get a big punishment, not a reward, no matter how small the cheat was.

### Question 70

A whistleblower is like a student who reports cheating and may get a reward for helping set things right.

### Question 71

A good team has clear rules, a captain, practice time, check-ups, and a way to raise your hand with a problem.

### Question 72

If you find a mistake in your homework, you fix it and learn from it, you do not hide it and hope the teacher never notices.

### Question 73

If you accidentally take something that is not yours, the honest path is to give it back and tell the truth.

### Question 74

If you find a wallet, you should return it right away, not wait a whole year to see if anyone asks.

### Question 75

If you order a meal and a truly separate dessert, the receipt shows both, and the dessert is clearly its own line.

### Question 76

You order the value meal and one extra cookie that is not in the meal, so the receipt shows the meal plus one cookie.

### Question 77

If a repair comes with free fixes, but something brand new breaks and needs a whole new repair, that new repair can be billed separately.

### Question 78

Putting a new cover on the same book does not make it a different book.

### Question 79

The correct answer is like buying two clearly different items and having each listed correctly on one honest receipt.

### Question 80

If you see something wrong, tell a trusted adult the right way instead of yelling, hiding, or changing things on your own.

### Question 81

If one note says 'already part of another item' and another says 'you already turned this in,' the first is unbundling and the second is a duplicate.

### Question 82

Counting the toys on the shelf against the list is the best way to notice the same toy was written down twice.

### Question 83

You cannot write 'separate' on the form unless the work really was separate and you can prove it.

### Question 84

If you get two of the same toy by mistake, you return the extra one to whoever it belongs to.

### Question 85

When a menu has a combo meal and individual items, you order the combo unless there is a real reason to buy one item on its own.
